record.original_question: (M. Bialy) Are there multi-dimensional convex billiards, other than e llipsoids, having invariant hypersurfaces in the phase space? Same question f or multi-dimensional outer billiards. A common feature of families of integrable maps is that they commute (Bianchi permutability). 17 Consider two confocal ellipses: the billiard reflections define two tra nsformations on the set of oriented lines that intersect both ellipses. These transformations commute, see [209]. The converse was recently proved by A. Glutsyuk [89], as a consequence of his classification of 4 -reflective complex planar billiards. For outer billiards, an analogous theorem is that if the outer billiard tr ansformations on two nested curves commute then the curves are concentric homothetic ellipse s [205]. It would be interesting to find a proof of Glutsyuk's result via a more geometric approach of [20 5]. In higher dimensions (greater than two), the billiard transformatio ns, induced by two confocal ellip- soids, commute as well (see, e.g., [64]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \ge 3$ be a smooth strictly convex bounded domain. The billiard map $T_\Omega$ acts on the phase space $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ of oriented lines intersecting $\Omega$ (equivalently, on inward unit vectors based at $\partial\Omega$) by the standard law of elastic reflection: an incoming oriented line hits $\partial\Omega$ at a point $p$ and is reflected so that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection with respect to the outward normal at $p$. An invariant hypersurface for $T_\Omega$ is a smooth codimension-one submanifold $\Sigma \subset \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ with $T_\Omega(\Sigma) = \Sigma$.

It is classical that if $\Omega$ is an ellipsoid, then $T_\Omega$ admits a foliation by invariant hypersurfaces (the families of lines tangent to confocal quadrics).

Question (a): Do there exist smooth strictly convex bounded domains $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 3$, other than ellipsoids, such that the billiard map $T_\Omega$ possesses an invariant hypersurface in its phase space?

Question (b): Analogously, let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be a smooth strictly convex bounded domain and let $T_K^{\text{out}}$ denote its outer (dual) billiard map, defined on the exterior of $K$ via the symplectic structure: for a point $x$ outside $K$, $T_K^{\text{out}}(x)$ is the reflection of $x$ through the point of tangency of the (suitably defined) supporting affine hyperplane to $K$ from $x$. Are there examples of such $K$, other than ellipsoids, for which $T_K^{\text{out}}$ admits an invariant hypersurface in phase space?
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains largely open for inner (Birkhoff) billiards in dimensions ≥ 3: classical Berger–Gruber rigidity shows that only ellipsoids admit convex caustics, but the broader existence of invariant hypersurfaces in phase space (not necessarily corresponding to caustics) is unresolved, and no non-ellipsoidal examples are known. For the outer (symplectic) billiard version, recent work (2025) of Bialy–Tabachnikov on symplectically self-polar convex bodies provides the first non-trivial examples of invariant hypersurfaces beyond ellipsoids, partially answering the outer-billiard part.

status_evidence.title: Outer billiards of symplectically self-polar convex bodies
status_evidence.snippet: Symplectically self-polar convex bodies provide the first non-trivial examples of invariant hypersurfaces for the outer billiard map, in contrast with Birkhoff billiards in higher dimensions where only ellipsoids have caustics.
status_evidence.claim: Non-ellipsoidal invariant hypersurfaces exist for the outer billiard map (symplectically self-polar bodies), partially resolving the outer-billiard question.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in Billiards and Quantitative Symplectic Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: There are no examples of invariant hypersurfaces besides ellipsoids in higher-dimensional Birkhoff billiards.
status_evidence.claim: The inner-billiard version remains open with no known non-ellipsoidal examples.
